subject.title: fix(security): bound plugin manifest reads in audit deep scan

question: Should deep security audits permanently cap installed-plugin package.json reads at 1 MiB and reject symlink or non-regular manifest targets while continuing with a manifest_parse_error warning?
rationale: The implementation is technically sound, but selecting the accepted manifest size and filesystem target policy changes a security boundary and requires owner intent rather than automated judgment.

options.title: Approve the 1 MiB boundary
options.body: Accept the proposed cap and regular-file-only policy, preserving the existing warning-and-directory-scan fallback for rejected manifests.

options.title: Align with the shared manifest boundary
options.body: Request a narrow revision that centralizes the package.json limit and file-opening policy with the repository's canonical plugin manifest boundary helpers and adds exact-limit and unsafe-target tests.

recommendation.title: Approve the 1 MiB boundary
recommendation.body: Accept the proposed cap and regular-file-only policy, preserving the existing warning-and-directory-scan fallback for rejected manifests.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced the affected code-safety audit path and are the strongest available feature-history owner for its intended fallback semantics.
